articleTitle: Machine Learning as a Support Tool for Early Diagnosis in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of the Literature - Scopus
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is “a developmental disability caused by differences in the brain [1]”. With this background, the need arises to find a support tool for early diagnosis in children with autism, where machine learning and deep learning algorithms are currently available. In addition, it can be noted that it is important to have “current knowledge of the subject [2, p. 98]”, and as an initial step, the agile framework for systematic reviews of literature in formative research was used, and a thematic index was established, identifying variables and levels of variation. Likewise, the searches were semantically structured and the search scripts related to the search sprints were developed. As a result, 143 and 189 articles per sprint were found, and 6 papers that are common in the search sprint A and B were selected, which serve as the first reference in a research plan.

articleTitle: Agile Framework for Systematic Reviews of Literature in Formative Research
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Currently, it is important to note that formative research can be used as a strategy in the teaching process [1], and it is possible to avoid “the parceling of content into minimum units [1]” in class subjects. In parallel, systematic literature reviews [2] can be integrated into the teaching-learning process in all areas of knowledge, such as engineering, education [2] and others, combining them as a pedagogical strategy [1] in the learning process formative research in the classroom [1]. Also, it is necessary to highlight that the agile framework was applied, which is composed of 3 main events [3], [4]: planning, development and review, in a case study to elaborate the state of the art on topics related to the “disorder of the autism spectrum (ASD)” and “machine learning” (ML).

articleTitle: Engineering with a Gender Perspective in Higher Education at a Spanish University
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The initiatives undertaken to promote gender perspective in Engineering and Architecture at the Escuela Politécnica Superior de Zamora (EPSZ) of the University of Salamanca (USAL) and in the province of Zamora are presented. Two specific actions were implemented. The first action focused on the EPSZ university community, including students and faculty members. A self-diagnostic process was conducted by applying a questionnaire to the EPSZ educational community. Based on the results, a discussion forum was organized with the active participation of both faculty and students. This action aimed to address the gender gap within the field. The second action targeted society as a whole, emphasizing engaging pre-university students and fostering their interest in Engineering and Architecture. Participating female teachers and researchers developed videos showcasing the resolution of engineering challenges and learning situations related to materials and everyday scenarios. Additionally, short videos were prepared to feature female engineering students from EPSZ sharing their educational experiences at the school, as well as presentations by graduate engineers and technical architects highlighting their professional journeys. This second action aimed to inspire vocations in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) careers while creating relatable female role models for girls, boys, and young people.

articleTitle: Indicators to Measure Competence “2.3. Engaging with Citizens Through Digital Technologies” of the DigComp Model in the Context of Active Aging
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In active aging, it is necessary for older adults to have digital skills, and if they do not have them, they must be able to acquire them. To do this, it is necessary to measure and create appropriate training plans, but in many cases there are no measurement indicators. This happens when talking about the competence “2.3. Engaging with citizens through digital technologies” of the DigComp model in older adults. For this reason, this study proposes situations and units of measurement that allow evaluating this competence in older adults, all of them prepared by the expert judgment methodology.

articleTitle: The Gender Gap in Secondary and High School Students in STEM Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The gender gap in STEM vocations among high school students still remains a troubling reality. Several studies indicate that students in general have less interest in science and technology subjects, and this disparity is even more distinguishable among female students. In fact, the aforementioned gender gap in STEM begins to manifest itself at an early age and worsens during adolescence. This is why in this study a comprehensive research was carried out to analyze the factors that contribute to the gender gap in STEM careers. This allowed the identification of effective measures to increase women's participation in these fields. One of the suggested solutions is the implementation of practical workshops, in which female figures play a key role. These workshops are used to demonstrate students that there are numerous role models nearby who can motivate and encourage them to explore and develop their interest on the field of science and technology. By providing said opportunities and role models, our aim is to build their confidence and confidence, and provide them with the necessary tools to take advantage of all the opportunities that the STEM field has to offer.

articleTitle: DigComp as a reference framework for skills and competencies in digital environments
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: DigComp was created by the European Commission as a reference framework for skills and competencies necessary to be competitive in digital environments and this study aims to analyze whether or not it is really being used. To do this, this study makes a bibliometric analysis of DigComp in Scopus, one of the main scientific databases, in order to find out what the impact of this tool is in the scientific world and where it is being produced, which shows if is actually being used or not. This analysis is carried out with the Bibliometrix tool and the documents that are analyzed are those published in this database until 2022, thereby demonstrating that DigComp is consolidating as a reference framework since its use is expanding at a good pace in the scientific world and not only within Europe, but it is also coming to be used outside of Europe.

articleTitle: Use of Audiovisual Media in the Teaching-Learning Process of Mathematics
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The purpose of the study was to determine the incidence of audiovisual media as a methodological strategy in the teaching-learning process of mathematics, through the use of technological tools by fifth-year students of Basic General Education. For the selection of the research subjects, a parallel 5th year of basic education was intentionally selected, within which 42 students were worked. Students were given an input test, the intervention using audiovisual material, and an output test. To verify the validity of the input and output test, a validation form was sent to three experts. Then a pilot test of the tests was carried out and Cronbach's Alpha was calculated to verify the reliability of the results. Based on the results, we can say that there are statistically significant differences between the input and output test scores. That is, the gain obtained in the exit test after the application of the intervention was significant, with a p value less than 0.05.

articleTitle: Proposals for the Development of the Digital Competence of University Teachers: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article analyzes the implementation of various proposals for the development of the digital competence of university professors and the strengthening of their pedagogical practices by enabling the diversification of their strategies and methodologies, as they face the challenges in a media society in constant transformation. A systematic literature review based on the PRISMA model was carried out to identify the main findings reported on the concept of digital competence, innovations and their use in the pedagogical practices of university teachers. The document search was carried out in the Redalyc, Dialnet, Scopus and Web of Science databases during the period of 2017–2021. The final sample of 26 studies was selected based on quality and relevance criteria. The results indicate the importance of digital competence to promote digital empowerment, in addition to the identification of the needs to generate proposals for digital teacher trainings and their pedagogical integration in the daily practices in the classroom.

articleTitle: Activities to Celebrate International Day of Women and Girls in Science
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This communication presents an activity carried out within the Physics course of the Chemical Engineering degree with the aim, on the one hand, of encouraging students to attend an event organized by the Equality Commission of the School of Engineering to celebrate the International Day of Women and Girls in Science and, on the other hand, to know the students' opinion about the aspects discussed in the colloquium, in which gender-related issues were dealt with.

articleTitle: The Use of ICT and Learning Styles in University Students from the Lambayeque Department
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)

authors.preferredName: María De Los Angeles Guzmán Valle

abstract: The present descriptive-correlational and cross-sectional quantitative study aims to determine the relationship between the use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) and the learning styles of university students from universities in Lambayeque, Peru. Making use of a non-experimental design, it is shown that the use of ICTs is positively and significantly related to learning styles, recognizing the importance it has in current academic training, hence the need to impact on work with ICTs, combining activities that allow each learning style to be reinforced by analysis and synthesis, collaborative learning, tasks that also encourage critical and reflective thinking regarding the information obtained from various platforms

articleTitle: Factors to Take into Account when Selecting and Implementing Business Simulators
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: aThis study pointed out the key factors to take into account when selecting and implementing business simulators. Through a literary review, the factors to be taken into account in this decision were identified, a causal analysis was carried out among experts through fuzzy cognitive maps and the results were processed with the FCMappers software, obtaining as key factors “Attitude”, “Perceived Usefulness” and “Intention”, and discarding security and privacy in the use of the simulator as a key factor in this decision.

articleTitle: Innovation Potential as a New Element in University Theses
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)

authors.preferredName: Sergio Rafael B. Del Carpio Hernández

abstract: Few theses drive technological development, and even fewer contribute to innovation. This is partly due to a gap in the structure of research reports. This study aims to propose the inclusion of “Innovation Potential” (IP) as a new element to bridge this gap in thesis structures, aligning with the open innovation model. Qualitative research was conducted to develop a tool for evaluating the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of theses. This was complemented by a quantitative approach to identify the most frequent TRL and IP levels. The sample included specialized literature and 354 undergraduate and postgraduate theses from a local university. The results showed that the theses predominantly fall into TRL1 and TRL2, highlighting the need to integrate IP into thesis structures. It was concluded that the IP should be placed in either the Results or Recommendations sections.

articleTitle: Literacy and Innovation Through Testing, Strategic Analysis and Debate on Artificial Intelligence Tools: Experience-IA in Journalism at University of Malaga
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper presents the approach and results of Experienc-IA, a project developed as part of a course on strategic planning, innovation, and foresight in the Journalism degree program at the University of Málaga in the 2022–23 academic year. With the pretext of implementing the SWOT-CAME applied research approach seen in the course, the project focuses on a common theme that is essential to reflect on and educate professionals and future professionals today: Artificial Intelligence (AI). First, each student conducts a user test and a SWOT analysis on a specific AI tool. Later, we do several face-to-face sessions to share results and conduct an overall SWOT-CAME analysis. The outcome is a collaborative document that profiles and categorizes over 40 generative AI or information verification tools. The results show positive outcomes in terms of participation, academic performance, assessment of the tool usage experience, and students' perception of their learning.

articleTitle: Optimizing Datasets in the E-Learning Ecosystem A State-of-the-Art Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The rapid evolution of digital technology has ushered in a new era of education through E-Learning platforms. At the heart of this transformation lies the optimization of datasets, a pivotal practice that underpins personalized learning experiences, adaptive assessments, and insightful learning analytics. This Article introduces a comprehensive review that delves into the contemporary landscape of dataset optimization within the E-Learning ecosystem. By exploring the significance, challenges, methodologies, best practices, case studies, and future trends, this article aims to provide an encompassing understanding of the role that optimized datasets play in shaping the future of education. Through a synthesis of recent research, the abstract previews the insights that will be uncovered regarding the pivotal intersection between data-driven insights and pedagogical expertise in the realm of E-Learning.

articleTitle: Precautionary principle for students' data protection
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper underscores the critical importance of data protection strategies in educational institutions to prevent potential emotional, physical, and financial harm to students arising from data leaks due cybersecurity incidents. The data of different cybersecurity reports reveals that most incidents pertain to unauthorized disclosures of personal data, potentially leading to significant financial harm as this data can be traded on the black market, indicating an urgent need for enhanced data protection measures. Existing data regulations are deemed insufficient in mitigating these risks, highlighting a need for preventive (ethical) principles to augment legal frameworks. This manuscript introduces the precautionary principle as a potent ethical guideline to enhance student data protection treatment. By bolstering these data processes, it aims to prevent cybersecurity incidents or at least limit their adverse impacts. The paper offers an in-depth exploration of the problem and makes a compelling case for the precautionary principle as a social value for caring for students' futures.

articleTitle: Student Satisfaction on Flipped Learning in Postgraduate Level
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The objective of the research is to assess the effectiveness of flipped learning in postgraduate students in order to determine their level of satisfaction in the virtual, hybrid and new normal modality. The methodology used was a quantitative approach with a correlational scope. The instrument used was a questionnaire. The scale established for each item was of a Likert type. The participants were students of a postgraduate course in administration. Data analysis was performed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The main results are that flipped learning promotes the usefulness of the contents, increases motivation in academic training, and encourages collaborative work. The conclusion is that flipped learning promotes high student satisfaction and quality in academic training.

articleTitle: Promoting the Use of Virtual Schools Among Teachers
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The knowledge and implementation of new didactic strategies are essential for optimally developing all teaching work. Technological tools are crucial for this purpose. This document deals with an activity applied to 27 high school and professional level teachers to promote an approach and use of virtual reality through a platform with Metaverse elements. As a result, six teachers have applied this activity in their classes, and the rest agree on the utility they find in their platform, looking for the ideal moment to use it. In conclusion, it is undeniable that the experimentation and incorporation of new tools benefit the students by facilitating new learning models and also the teachers, who develop different skills to enhance their professional and personal development.

articleTitle: Analysis of Institutional Policies on the Use of Chat GPT in Peruvian Universities
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the institutional policies established in the intellectual property regulations of universities regarding the use of artificial intelligence in academic work. The study adopts a qualitative descriptive approach and is of a documentary type. The technique of document analysis and the selected instrument for data collection is the documentary analysis matrix. The results revealed that, up to the present moment, higher education institutions have not established any intellectual property regulations or a code of ethics to govern the use of artificial intelligence in academic production.

articleTitle: Towards the Hybrid Transformation of University Teaching: A Hyflex Experience in Teacher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper presents an experience in higher education where a hybrid and flexible methodology (Hyflex) is implemented. Unlike other models, this experience combined face-to-face classes with asynchronous activities in a virtual classroom. The flexibility allowed students to choose between customized projects and more traditional study units. The results showed high satisfaction and positive evaluation from the students, along with high academic performance, regardless of the selected learning path.

articleTitle: UMCE Virtual Practicum Campus: Installation, Implementation and Challenges 2020 - 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The following document showcases the transformation experienced at Metropolitan University of Education Sciences (herein UMCE, the Spanish acronym) a pedagogical university in Santiago, Chile, specifically in the area of educational practicum processes. Since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019, a virtual practicum community was established, which now serves as a repository for e-portfolios, a student self-learning  area, and a self-training space for pre-service teachers and tutors,  among others. Currently, 90 percent of the university's programs actively participate in this virtual community. It is projected that by 2025, all undergraduate programs will be integrated into the virtual practicum community.

articleTitle: Implementation and learning impact of Plickers in engineering education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Engineering education in the last decade has shown an evolution in teaching methods, since the most present is the traditional expository teaching, where the student participates passively, while the main or active actor is the teacher, with the pandemic revolutionized education using digital tools to support teaching in any context, with regard to engineering education took a boom and in recent years we have found studies where different tools have been implemented with or without the use of technology where active learning takes place and where the role of the student changes drastically. The objective of this work is to present the implementation of Plickers in the environment of engineering education applied to the teaching of manufacturing processes where the student's perception and interaction with this tool is presented and thus demonstrate that the implementation of tools such as Plickers has an impact on active learning in the engineering student and a greater motivation and participation.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Predictive Mode of Student Difficulties, Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: With the arrival of the internet, huge volumes of data have been generated in several repositories and websites such is the case for social media Twitter, which registers exponential growth due to constant user interactions causing much research focused on several fields of study including the automation of processing such data. Concerning the field of education, there is an increment of studies that combines Big Data with the information derived from such a field of study through the development and implementation of algorithms that utilize different Data Mining techniques, Natural Language Processing, and Machine Learning. The main contribution of this research consists of the development of an algorithm to predict college students’ difficulties, reported on the social media Twitter by using a basic artificial neural network, creating 11 models with different characteristics to identify the model that reaches higher accuracy, and comparing the results with other developed algorithms. The model built on basic artificial neural networks reached 77,78% accuracy, thus, it is considered an acceptable model for the case study.

articleTitle: Blended Learning based Artificial Intelligence Mapping to Optimize Learning Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Blended Learning is gaining popularity as artificial intelligence and technology are integrated into education. This research provides a bibliometric analysis of Blended Learning based Artificial Intelligence in Education. This study employs bibliometrics to identify field tendencies, influential authors, highly-cited articles, and theme clusters. Data collection used Scopus.com to select relevant sources that found 439 documents. The scholarly articles and conference papers are analyzed to disclose publication patterns and research output for Blended Learning-based AI in Education. The research show lists the top publication country, prolific authors, and highly cited publications determined by bibliometric analysis. The research shows that Blended Learning and AI education research are interdisciplinary; consequently, co-authorship networks and collaborative patterns are investigated. Thematic clusters and term co-occurrence maps uncover themes and emerging trends. These insights assist in identifying research gaps, opportunities, and prospective fields of study. This research promotes Blended Learning based AI in education. To summarize, AI-enhanced learning environments by recognizing researchers and comprehending the field's evolution. The findings assist academics, educators, and policymakers collaborate on AI education development and make evidence-based decisions.

articleTitle: Students Survey Results with Arduino IoT Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Considering the current post-pandemic scenario, the experiments carried out during the virtual classes, allowed the evaluation of results that allow an extension of the face-to-face model, in this way the results of this study present the evidence about a process of application of the cloud platforms used during virtual classes to the internet of things, especially considering the moment of the pandemic, which provided many possibilities for renewal and adaptation. The results of this study demonstrated the capacity and feasibility of using the development platform known as Arduino Cloud, in which it was possible to demonstrate and apply surveys with students. The results presented demonstrate the opinion of the participants, considering their personal experience for the application in projects for different types of studies, the values evaluated as quantitative demonstrate an acceptance for the use of the tool, while the values classified as qualitative, after consolidated, identify the points positives and negatives for using this type of platform. The results allow a contribution to the area of scientific research, providing new paths and helping in the teaching and learning process with the presented technologies.

articleTitle: Active Pedagogy as a Tool for Innovation: Perspectives from Professional Development in Teacher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article analyzes the organization, structure and implementation of a training course called Approaches to active pedagogy offered by the Department of Continuing Education at National University of Education, UNAE. It served 400 Ecuadorian teachers, who work at the elementary and high school levels. The purpose of the course was to expand and strengthen teachers' knowledge on issues related to active pedagogy as a possibility to generate processes of educational innovation through a diversity of strategies. The results obtained show a dynamization of the training processes and the satisfaction of teachers in topics that allow them to transform their teaching practices.

articleTitle: Application of the STEM Methodology in the Development of a Closed-Loop Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The STEM methodology has been applied in different study approaches, covering different areas such as arts, internet of things, computational thinking, among others. In this paper, two necessary approaches are addressed for the implementation of a closed-loop control system. The first approach (programming) is directly related to the software implementation and the second approach addresses the hardware instrumentation part. Both approaches are developed in a practical teaching case, from a STEM Maker workshop which consisted of 15 sessions with duration 2 hours each one. Each session consisted of 4 stages: Stage 1 (Theoretical concepts), Stage 2 (Practical Example), Stage 3 (Practice) and Stage 4 (challenge). Through these four stages, the development of skills of the attendees in the areas of programming and electronics was encouraged, applying the STEM Maker strategy. From some evaluation instruments, data was collected about the development of skills of the assistants in the implementation of software and hardware instrumentation, acquired in the STEM Maker workshop. The results indicated that approximately 70% of the workshop attendees developed the necessary skills to propose solutions to problems in their current context where the application of programming and/or electronics intervenes. The product obtained from the practice is described as a temperature control which integrates a feedback signal, this system has a wide field of applications which allowed the students of the STEM Maker workshop to achieve a project related to the individual context of each one.

articleTitle: Information and Communication Technology Competencies of Incoming University Students: A Case Study of Universities in the Lambayeque Region, Peru 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)

authors.preferredName: María de los Ángeles Guzmán Valle

abstract: This cross-sectional descriptive quantitative study diagnoses the competencies in information and communication technologies (ICTs) of university students entering different universities in Lambayeque, Peru. Using a non-experimental design, the perception that students have regarding the management of their ICT competencies is determined. The findings showed that most students considered themselves not entirely competent with respect to the knowledge and use of computer tools, hence the need to forge these skills for information management and knowledge management.

articleTitle: Evolution of Digital Skills in ICT in the Educational and Business Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article shows the evolution of ICT from its beginnings to the present, as well as its growing influence in the educational and business fields. The objective is to analyze the evolution of ICT and its progressive development in the educational and business sectors. A review of the academic literature and specialized sources on the subject was carried out through searches in electronic databases and the most relevant and recent studies were selected. Aspects such as the emergence of ICT, its evolution over time and its integration in the educational and business fields are considered. The outcomes achieved reveal that ICTs have undergone a notable evolution from their origin to the present. Initially, they were limited to basic data processing tools, but over time they have incorporated new functionalities and have become a fundamental part of our society. In the educational field, ICTs have transformed the way of teaching and learning. Likewise, they have allowed the creation of virtual learning environments and the development of new pedagogical methodologies. Meanwhile, in the business field, ICTs have changed the processes of communication and business management. They have optimized operational efficiency, facilitating data-driven decision-making; besides allowing the expansion of business through globalization and electronic commerce.

articleTitle: The Webcam Eye Tracking as a Tool to Increase PX with Serious Games for Learning: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Serious Games (SG) for learning have been adopted by educational institutions as a virtual strategy for the contribution of hard and soft skills, however, the real-time monitoring of the use of this teaching resource are still not sufficiently studied. The existing research indicates, usually in an isolated way, contributions from the use of SG, obtained from experimental techniques or exclusively qualitative methods. As well, considering how much the new technologies based on the behavioral study make it possible to discover how the learner reacts at the exact moment of learning, this work monitored the Player Experience (PX) during the use of a simulator in a business environment by 7 students and 3 professors from the Federal Institute of Education, Science and Technology of Rio Grande do South not Brazil. Supported by a webcam eye tracking (ET) device, the fixation heat maps on the screen provided an understanding of the areas of greatest interest and fixation of the eye of each player at different times of the proposed game. Complementarily, with pre- and post-test questionnaire, it was possible to identify both very particular behaviors and collective patterns among the players, related to the influence of aspects such as design elements of the tutorial and the game, previous knowledge and the definition of the performance strategy. The results show that the use of the ET webcam can be very useful in evaluating the capabilities and design elements of the GS, both for those who use them in the teaching process and for game developers to, in the end, offer a better PX.

articleTitle: Pedagogical Innovation: Integrating MOOCs in Regular Classrooms
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper highlights the pedagogical challenges required to incorporate Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) in teaching-learning at the undergraduate level. This paper is based on the focus group study of the students who undertook the MOOCs. Focus group is used with the objective to uncover why students feel and perceive things in a particular manner along with institutional arrangement to make the process smoother. The case lets discussed in the paper provides unique insights into students’ perception of these new pedagogical tools. The summer MOOCs journey highlights the challenges of handling dropouts (MOOC completion rate), the success of decreased specialization switches, and productive engagement. MOOCs embedded in the course (SWAYAM) exposed students to various pedagogical experiences which helped them in concept clarity and understanding. The challenging part was to select relevant courses or units in the course which suits the subject requirement along with making institutional arrangement to facilitate the same. It resulted in students doing multiple online and certification courses.

articleTitle: Emotion Detection Methods Appropriate for Evaluating User Experience in Virtual Learning Platforms in Spanish: Expert Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article addresses the importance of evaluating the user experience in virtual learning platforms in Spanish through the detection of emotions, and presents the perspectives of experts in the field. In the context of the growing popularity of virtual education, understanding how emotions influence the user experience becomes crucial to improve the effectiveness and design of these platforms. To carry out this research, a survey was conducted with a group of experts in the field, who provided their views on the most appropriate emotion detection methods for this purpose. The results obtained from the answers provided by the experts are analyzed and discussed. Among the most relevant findings, the importance of employing emotion detection techniques that are accurate and non-invasive to ensure an effective evaluation of the user experience is highlighted. In conclusion, this study provides an enriching insight into the most appropriate emotion detection methods for evaluating user experience in virtual learning platforms in Spanish. The findings presented contribute to the understanding of how emotions can influence the effectiveness of these platforms, which is fundamental for the design of more satisfying and successful educational experiences in the digital dominion. Combining questionnaires with these technological approaches presents an unbeatable forthcoming opportunity.

articleTitle: Curricular Internationalization: Use and Benefits of Information and Communication Technology Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The internationalization of the curriculum aims to foster international integration and cooperation, and to enhance the quality of academic programs. It entails a global vision that enables the creation of meaningful experiences that transcend the classroom or the national context. However, in Latin America, internationalization programs have limited access. Information and communication technologies (ICTs) offer an opportunity to break these constraints and make internationalization more accessible. In this regard, this paper evaluates the impact of using ICTs in internationalization strategies on the number of participants. We analyze the outcomes of internationalization projects conducted in the first call for this type of initiative in both face-to-face and distance modalities at the Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja. We employ generalized linear models to evaluate whether there is a significant difference in the participation of faculty and students with and without the use of ICTs and across different study modalities. We find that the use of ICTs leads to a significantly higher participation of students from both the host and partner institutions. Moreover, our results show a significantly higher participation of students in the distance mode and with a higher proportion of international students. In conclusion, our work demonstrates that the use of ICTs significantly improves the impact on the number of students involved in internationalization strategies. Future research should assess to what extent internationalization initiatives that rely on ICTs can meet the educational objectives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Speaking Skills in PALP Students: A Qualitative Study on the Implementation of the Cake App as a Mobile Learning Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The research aims to describe the practical utilization of the Cake app within PALP, elucidate the gains observed in students' speaking skills through its medium, and identify the challenges encountered by both students and mentors while employing the app as a learning aid. This qualitative descriptive research involved six PALP participants who willingly volunteered for the study. Data collection methods included interviews and documentations, which were analyzed through data logging, anecdotes, vignettes, and data coding processes. The study's findings indicate that the Cake app plays a crucial role in facilitating students' language development by enhancing their speaking skills and fostering a keen interest in learning. As mobile learning continues to evolve, the Cake app stands as a promising asset to enrich language education and cultivate a dynamic and interactive learning environment for language learners.

articleTitle: Information and Data Literacy: An Analysis of Digital Skill in University Students
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The present research is based on the use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in the teaching-learning process in university students. In addition, the inclusion of artificial intelligence in digital skills is analyzed as a relevant factor in the current context. The study is carried out with higher level students and is quantitative. The results of the analysis of the Information and data literacy competence allow us to identify that it is possible to improve the digital skills in the participants because they were placed at an advanced level despite the fact that the students are from the computing area, however it is necessary to work with real and complex scenarios to reach the expert level.

articleTitle: Peer Assessment Experience as Summative Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Co-evaluation is a didactic technique that develops students’ deep learning and promotes formative evaluation with immediate feedback. In addition, it reduces the teacher's workload, especially in large groups. However, the use of peer assessment results as a measure of summative assessment is still under discussion. This paper describes a peer assessment experience with monitoring of the students' opinion regarding the grade received. Teachers intervened to review the submitted works that aroused the greatest evaluators‧ discrepancy. The results show that about 40% of the ratings issued by peers are not sufficiently reliable as measures of summative evaluation. The calculation of an internal meta-evaluation variable would allow teachers to estimate the quality of each peer assessment and to improve the reliability of the summative assessment.

articleTitle: Social Networks as Spaces to Generate Learning Communities Among University Students
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Social networks are tools that are increasingly used by university students to share information, communicate with friends and family, meet people and learn more about topics of interest. The objective of this learning experience was to build a virtual learning community through social networks to generate knowledge among users with a common interest. Forty students of the Bachelor's Degree in Education Sciences of a public university in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico, participated. The work was based on project-based learning that articulates experience and action. As a result of this experience, eleven virtual learning communities were designed to address academic, emotional health, sexual health and animal protection issues. The work developed during a semester allowed linking the theoretical knowledge reviewed in the sessions with their digital skills from a techno-pedagogical perspective. Among the most significant findings was the diversity of technological resources used by the students to design their social network, as well as the number of members and the interaction process generated by the publications. The didactic route used in this experience can be replicated in other academic spaces at both higher and middle school levels.

articleTitle: AI's Role in the Academic Writing Process: An Exploration for University Students
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has begun to play a significant role in the academic writing process for university students. This study examines, through a systematic scope literature review, how the integration of artificial intelligence can benefit students in their task of writing academic papers. First, the use of artificial intelligence as an additional tool in academic writing is analyzed, including automatic content generation, grammar and spelling correction, as well as the suggestion of structures and arguments. Generative artificial intelligence can act as a virtual assistant that provides support at every stage of the writing process, complementing students' knowledge and skills instead of replacing them. Students must be aware of possible risks and take precautions to ensure the integrity and originality of their work.

articleTitle: Internet Quota Subsidies: Evaluation of Policy Covid in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Internet quota subsidies are one policy of the Indonesian government in a pandemic era. This study aimed to find out about utilization in higher education. The study used a survey with a simple random sampling technique with 266 respondents. The method of data analysis used was descriptive quantitative. The quota subsidy is only 69.9%, using 10 GB of 50 GB. This condition shows that the quota provided is not used up. Students use quota subsidies for lectures, research, webinars, and fun. Students do not use all the learning applications offered to their full potential.

articleTitle: Enrollment Level in Higher Education in Young People Aged 17 to 24, Perú 2010 – 2021
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)

authors.preferredName: María de los Ángeles Guzmán Valle

abstract: Education in Peru is increasingly showing better prospects, particularly due to the potential income to be earned. This research aims to determine the level of higher education among young people aged 17 to 24 in Peru from 2010 to 2021. To this end, we used data from INEI on higher education enrolments among young people, conducting a basic, quantitative, descriptive, and non-experimental investigation. It was concluded that there is an enrolment growth for both males at 1.5% and females at 2.3%, with females showing more interest in pursuing higher education. Rural enrolment is lower compared to urban areas, where urban enrolment doubles that of the rural areas. Higher education enrolments are similar at the coast and in the mountains, while in the jungle they are lower, representing half compared to the other regions.

articleTitle: Building a Sustainable E-Learning Ecosystem : Strategies for Long-Term Success
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The e-learning ecosystem has seen rapid growth and innovation in recent years, thanks to technological advances and changes in the education landscape. However, ensuring the sustainability of e-learning platforms and initiatives is essential to their long-term success and impact. This document explores the different components that contribute to a sustainable e-learning ecosystem, and proposes strategies to meet the challenges and foster growth.

articleTitle: Integration of Campus Virtual and Mobile Applications for an Enhanced Academic Experience
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In today's digital era, educational institutions are leveraging technology to enhance their teaching and learning processes. This technical paper focuses on the integration of a “Campus Virtual” platform based on Moodle and a mobile application using AppCRUE. The integration aims to centralize information, streamline communication, and improve notification management within the educational ecosystem. This paper provides an overview of the integration components, including services for calendar synchronization, autologin, sitemap generation, avatar retrieval, instant messaging, and grade notifications. The integration enables seamless data exchange between the Campus Virtual platform and mobile applications, empowering students, and teachers with enhanced educational management capabilities.

articleTitle: Digital Literacy for Migrant Women. «Más Que Emplea» Project
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In the Knowledge Society, mastery of digital competences is essential for all citizens. It is important to have skills that allow us to manage in a changing and hyper-connected digital environment in which certain vulnerable groups can be excluded because adequate mechanisms are not provided for technology to reach everyone equally without generating a double gap, both digital and social. For this reason, this research strives to design a digital literacy programme aimed at 699 migrant women in order to put into practice digital skills and tools that contribute to promoting their participation and exercising their rights on an equal footing in society by improving their basic digital competences.

articleTitle: Practical Results for IoT Virtual Classes with Wokwi Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Due to the pandemic period experienced in recent years, the classes needed adaptations, due to this need, studies were carried out on online tools which could collaborate for a remote experience closer to reality, in this way one of the evaluated possibilities, the Wokwi tool demonstrated It is feasible to present simulations and prototypes which allow an experience for students and teachers to present quick results without the need to use physical devices. This material presents the results of proposals used in the classroom and a personal assessment of the benefits and contribution of the Wokwi tool, which demonstrated the feasibility of using its main resources during classes on the Internet of Things. The experiments carried out were applied with some basic contents for the construction of solutions for the Internet of Things, presenting the main characteristics of the tool, the different options of devices and languages that can be used for the creation of projects, also addressing some positive and negative characteristics. observed during studies and experiments.

articleTitle: The Exchange of Information Perceived as a Mediating Effect Between the Advantages of Virtual Learning and the Intention to Continue Studying
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The study's objective was to establish the exchange of information perceived as a mediating effect between the advantages of virtual learning and the intention to continue studying. The research is non-experimental and quantitative; there was a sample of 106 Pre-Graduate university students. First, an Exploratory Factorial Analysis was conducted to condense the information in the original variables into smaller series; second, a Confirmatory Factorial Analysis was conducted, which made it possible to conduct the internal consistency tests of the model using non-parametric statistics, correlation and linear regression tests were conducted. It is concluded that the proposed model is robust, in addition, that the correlations that are deduced from the model have a non-parametric explanation in such a way that there is a high positive association between the advantages of learning in virtual modality, exchange of perceived information and the intention to continue with university studies. In addition, the mediation effect of the perceived information exchange is significant.

articleTitle: Piloting of a Scale to Measure Digital Skills Using Practical Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The article addresses the validation of an assessment instrument to measure digital skills in older adults from the perspective of active aging (AA). The construction of the scale is based on theoretical bases on AA in relation to the European framework of digital competences, as well as the criteria of experts. The authors highlight the importance of having a flexible and adaptable tool that allows knowing the level of activity and autonomy of the elderly with the technologies. The study included a sample of 34 older people who participated in a digital literacy workshop with a methodology based on the practical test, as well as exploratory factor analysis. The results of the pilot test show the validity and reliability of the first version of the instrument to assess the level of skills of this segment of the population.

articleTitle: Perceptions on the use of EVEA in University Faculty: A Comprehensive Study on the Effects of Activities and Learning Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Incorporation of technology in education has revolutionized the teaching and learning process. Among the tools and platforms developed to enhance education, EVEA (Entorno Virtual de Enseñanza y Aprendizaje) has gained significant interest. EVEA provides diverse activities and learning resources for interactive learning. As Universidad Nacional de Educación (UNAE) integrates EVEA into its academic programs, it becomes crucial to analyze the activities and learning resources employed by university faculty when designing virtual classrooms. The study employed a qualitative approach, with 41 participants from different majors. Findings reveal the most utilized activities are Tasks, facilitating assignment collection, feedback, and student accountability. Files and URLs were the primary learning resources used by professors. Furthermore, participants perceived EVEA as a valuable vehicle for accessing resources, flexible learning, and engaging students. On the other hand, challenges encompass technology disparities, digital skills, and student distractions. Lastly, recommendations entail thorough training, dedicated support platforms, and teacher collaboration to maximize EVEA's potential.

articleTitle: Transforming Education: Metaverse Challenges and Teacher Training - An Integrative Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The constant transformation in the field of education and pedagogical practices, resulting from the integration of new technologies, brings about new demands for teacher training. As the processes related to distance education become established, a new step emerges with the adoption of technological resources that allow immersion in virtual, augmented, and mixed realities, such as the metaverse. This article aims to map the main challenges encountered in the use of such technologies in teacher training. To do so, an integrative literature review was conducted on the main knowledge bases. The main findings indicate that there is a set of factors that should be considered and that influence teachers in the adoption of these technologies. It was also found that teacher training strategies need to be reconsidered, as traditional strategies are still being used, limiting the possibilities for learning in practice.

Author Keywords: Metaverse. Teacher training. Virtual Reality. Augmented Reality. Teacher education

articleTitle: Teacher Educational Innovation: A Systematic and Content Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Education is a process that must be accompanied by transformations to guarantee a relevant education for students. In this sense, innovation is a key factor that guarantees value to learning. Innovative education promotes progress, new knowledge and encourages research. Therefore, it was proposed to carry out a systematic and content review of the documents obtained with the use of the keywords “teacher”, “innovation” and “education” with a total of 373 documents obtained and analysed. Among the results obtained, it is necessary to highlight a clear link between innovation and the process of improving the curriculum, reflective practice and the use of active methodologies such as the flipped classroom and educational technology. In the future, we want to expand this study, analysing the content of the methodological headings and conclusions of the records.

articleTitle: Promoting Equality in Higher Education Computer Programming Courses Through Cooperative Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Every day we live with more technology and computer systems. It is widely known that this technology is not neutral and can harm citizens, specially women. A possible cause for this lack of neutrality could be the under-representation of women on development teams. Our hypothesis is that the motivation of female students could increase through the use of alternative didactic methodologies, specifically the cooperative learning, including the gender dimension in its design. This study describes and analyses the use of cooperative learning to teach computer programming courses in a higher education STEM discipline, the Math degree. The statistical evaluation of the perception of the students along two academic years was very positive, specially for the female students.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation in Music Education: Addressing Challenges in Technology-Enhanced Music Education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The study aims to examine the opportunities presented by technology in music education, such as personalized learning, interactive platforms, and access to extensive resources. Qualitative methods were used to conduct this research. The findings of this study reveal the plethora of opportunities that digital transformation offers in music education. Technology integration has the potential to foster creativity, promote collaborative learning, and enable individualized learning paths. However, the research also highlights significant challenges that need to be addressed, such as the need for professional development to support educators in making effective use of digital tools, ensuring equitable access to technology, and developing appropriate frameworks for the assessment and evaluation of technology-enhanced music learning. The study's contributions can help design effective strategies and policies that harness the potential of technology to create inclusive, engaging, and effective music learning environments. Ultimately, this work contributes to a broader discourse on digital transformation in education and lays the foundation for further research in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: A response to smartphone addiction among university populations in an emerging country, Piura - 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)

authors.preferredName: María de los Ángeles Guzmán Valle

abstract: In fact, the World Health Organisation has sounded the alarm about the dependence that digital technologies impose on human beings, distracting and damaging the normal development of their daily activities [1]. This warning is a consequence of the exponential and almost traumatic use of social networks, web communication, online communication, among others. Under these circumstances, the objective of the study was to find an answer to smartphone addiction in the university population of an emerging country - Peru 2023. In terms of methodology and due to the characteristics of the study, a quantitative approach was used, a descriptive non-experimental design, in which a total of 376 students from 4 universities representative of the Piura Region participated. The results of the study showed that one of the possible responses to smartphone addiction are precisely certain socio-demographic factors related to age, gender, level of education, as well as the use of this technological equipment is increasing and goes hand in hand with the emergence of new social interaction apps.

articleTitle: Having Fun and Teaching Learning English Outreach Project Evaluation UNAE Ecuador: A Quantitative Study in Virtual Education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This research evaluates the impact of the community outreach project called Having fun and teaching/learning English of the English teaching major (Pedagogía de los Idiomas Nacionales y Extranjeros PINE) at Universidad Nacional de Educación (UNAE). The project involved 800 children and was carried out in the 2021–2022 academic period. A quantitative methodology of data collection and analysis was used to evaluate the impact of the program. This evaluation assessed the perceptions of the children, student teachers from the PINE major, and their academic tutors. The research focuses on 1) children's language learning and skills development; 2) student teachers' professional development through the design implementation and didactic reflection; and 3) the impact of academic tutoring on professional teaching training. Based on the findings of this research, adjustments were made to the program to maximize English language teaching and learning in the virtual modality

articleTitle: Analyses of the Use of the Forum Resource on University Virtual Campuses. A Comparative Study Between the Years Before and During Covid19
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper presents the results obtained from the structure and context of the forum resource from Moodle virtual platforms. Specifically, an analysis is carried out to detect didactic characteristics in the forum design inherent to the subjects of postgraduate degrees at the University of La Laguna during the academic years 2016–2017 until the academic year 2020–2021. This communication represents only a part of a broad study in which different resources and characteristic elements of virtual classrooms are reviewed. The results obtained, thanks to the methodological approach carried out, show differences in the academic years following the impact of COVID-19 on the forum resource and obtain evidence of distinctive characteristics of didactic design in forum resources on virtual platforms.

articleTitle: Using Educaplay as a Digital Tool to Improve Reading Comprehension
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The incorporation of ICT in the teaching-learning process has become a fundamental tool for the training and evaluation of students. In the present research they have been used to reinforce the communicative skills of the subject of language and literature, in students of third year of EGB. For this purpose, the digital tool educaplay is used, which, thanks to its benefits and ease of use, is presented as an excellent option. As results, it is observed that the vast majority of students have electronic devices and internet access; at the same time, they express their pleasure in the application of interactive games to improve their learning in a fun way, being the most popular ones: matching columns, crossword puzzles and word search puzzles. In addition, thanks to the fact that it is an intuitive platform, students can develop the activities without help, thus achieving the acquisition of reading, writing and reading comprehension skills.

articleTitle: Enhancing Meeting Management and Voting in Higher Education Institutions Using Moodle
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth exploration of how Moodle, a popular learning management system, has been utilized to manage meetings and conduct anonymous voting in university committees and academic boards. By leveraging Moodle's course tools, a dedicated space for meeting documentation management was implemented. To address the lack of complete anonymity in the original “feedback” module, a modified version was developed to enable anonymous voting. The paper details the modifications made to the feedback module, the anonymous voting process, user satisfaction, and future integration plans. The solution has received positive feedback from users, with over 500 anonymous and about 1,000 public votes conducted by 102 committees in the past two years.

articleTitle: Educational Applications on Smartphone for Virtual Laboratories in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper focuses on the transition of virtual lab to the smartphone platform. It presents an overview of the virtual lab work, and highlights the concept of virtual lab on smartphone. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the proposed approach. Afterwards, a set of challenges for the development of virtual labs is presented. Solutions for these challenges are then presented alongside their implementation in a developed virtual lab application. In particular, the virtual lab applications employed are concrete mix design, fluid friction test, machine learning lab, control simulation and permeability testing.

articleTitle: Strengthening Educational Inclusion: The Interaction Between Bloom's Taxonomy, Universal Design for Learning, Habits of Mind and Technology in Educational Praxis
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Currently, educational compromise is intimately related to the transformation “of’ and “from” schools. This transformation happens when educational praxis changes through contextualized actions, thus achieving quality in teaching. In this sense, the use of information and communication technologies is essential. Emotional education also plays a fundamental role in achieving a more complete, fair and inclusive education. To achieve this transformation, throughout this innovation proposal, we analyze the skills required by the society of the 21st century. These skills are related to teaching children to think, so that in the future they will be able to solve problems as critically and creatively as possible. To this end, we have reviewed the literature related to habits of mind, Bloom's taxonomy and the aspects underlying Universal Design for Learning (UDL), paying special attention to connecting the principles that all of them propose with technological educational resources. In this sense, we offer a synthesis of these essential skills that teachers should take into consideration in the classroom to achieve a more inclusive education and society.

articleTitle: Information Technologies in Quality Management in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The use of Information Technologies (IT) has played an increasingly important role in quality management in higher education. This article examines the impact of IT on improving quality management processes and promoting academic excellence in higher education institutions. IT offers a range of tools and solutions that enable higher education institutions to collect, analyze, and interpret relevant data for assessing and monitoring quality in higher education. Through learning management systems, online assessment platforms, and data analysis software, institutions can obtain accurate and real-time insights into student performance, teaching effectiveness, and student satisfaction. Furthermore, IT enables the implementation of quality management systems based on international standards, such as ISO 9001:2015, providing a structured framework for continuous improvement in higher education processes. These systems can facilitate the documentation of policies and procedures, the monitoring of performance indicators, and the conduct of internal and external audits, contributing to quality assurance and compliance with established standards. IT also plays a crucial role in communication and collaboration among the various stakeholders involved in quality management in higher education. Through online portals and platforms, students, faculty, administrators, and staff can share information, exchange feedback, and participate in decision-making processes, promoting a more participatory and transparent approach to quality management. However, it is important to emphasize that the effective implementation of IT in quality management requires a strategic approach and an institutional culture supportive of innovation. Higher education institutions must invest in suitable technological infrastructure, provide training and support to users, and ensure data security and privacy. IT plays a fundamental role in quality management in higher education by providing tools and solutions that contribute to the improvement of higher education processes, compliance with international standards, and effective communication among stakeholders. The strategic adoption of IT can drive academic excellence and student satisfaction, fostering a culture of quality in higher education institutions.

articleTitle: Why ChatGPT Isn't Introductory Programming Freshmen's Best Friend
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The emergence of ChatGPT brought a lot of controversy in society and academia due to the ease with which students can effortlessly perform work. This paper investigates whether a freshman student in an introductory programming unit using Python benefits from using ChatGPT, even as an aid. The methodology used was the application of three written tests of one semester - using Python programming language -, answered by ChatGPT (free version), analysed, and compared with a “good” solution of each one. Strangely, or maybe not, errors and problems were found in the solutions provided by ChatGPT that are the same ones that self-taught student (those who learn on YouTube and websites around the Internet world) make.

articleTitle: Adapting digital competence 2.1 from the DigCom Model in the context of active ageing
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The last two decades have been characterised by two phenomena: an ageing population and unprecedented technological progress. The ageing of the population has an impact on society and the economy, and the social inclusion of the elderly is one of the major challenges for advanced societies to avoid social segregation. The confident and critical use of information technologies for work, leisure and communication is one of the eight basic skills that every citizen should acquire, according to the European Parliament's recommendation on key competences for lifelong learning; digital competence is therefore considered a human right. However, there are few studies that analyse and promote the digital competences of older adults. The aim of this work is to adjust a DigCom-based digital competence model for active ageing (AA). Specifically, it presents an adaptation of competence 2.1, linked to communication and interaction between people using digital media, to the context of AA, showing the different levels of competence with contextualised examples.

articleTitle: Use of Canva as a Digital Tool for the Preparation and Filling of Electronic Invoices
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The use of technological tools nowadays has become a priority in different business areas. In this research we made use of the Canva tool, with the objective of establishing the teaching of the filling of electronic invoices and the adaptation of the models that the Canva platform brings to the company. It is also important to note that the company Recolplastic in which this research was developed has under its corporate responsibility to train entrepreneurs to obtain knowledge in the tax area, this time not only was trained in tax issues but in the parameterization and design of invoice models according to the tax regulations of Ecuador using one of the tools widely used in different fields of knowledge such as Canva.

articleTitle: Genially a Tool for Learning Mathematics
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Technology in the educational field has become a very useful resource and in the future indispensable, technological tools allow teachers and students to work with interactive resources that enliven the teaching-learning process. This, combined with innovative active strategies, creates dynamic, critical and reflective learning environments. In the Julio María Matovelle Educational Unit, the application of Genially was implemented as an active and dynamic tool, which has strengthened links between the teacher and the students, creating friendly learning environments, resulting in students feeling more interest in the subject and improving the teaching-learning process, through gamification and the inverted classroom methodology, concluding that Genially is a tool that allows improving the academic performance of students, encouraging interest in the subject, improving relationships between students and teachers, developing conceptual, attitudinal, procedural, technological and emotional competencies.

articleTitle: An Experience to Introduce the Planning and Time Management Competence in an Engineering Degree
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This paper presents an experience of development and integration of the competence of Planning and Time Management through two consecutive subjects for engineering students. With this objective in mind, a simplified variant of existing techniques has been implemented to allow students to approach the subject without appreciable overload.

articleTitle: Model of Educational Context Diagnosis: Building Bridges Towards Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In an increasingly complex, interconnected, and dynamic world, education plays a fundamental role in individual and social development. That is why this article presents a socio-critical diagnostic model designed for elementary education teachers, which addresses five key dimensions: political, cultural, economic, health-related, familial, and technological. The model is based on a critical pedagogy perspective and has been validated by experts from four countries. Its potential lies in enabling teachers to investigate and identify weaknesses and areas for improvement within an educational environment, thereby fostering the creation of educational intervention plans in collaboration with parents, administrators, and the broader educational community. The model serves as a tool to guide the construction of more democratic, intercultural, and supportive educational contexts.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality to Improve Attention in Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: Nowadays, schools seek to promote inclusive education in which mainstream classrooms can meet the needs of all students. In this sense, information and communication technologies are presented as an additional educational tool in the teaching process of students at different educational stages. Within these technological tools, the use of Augmented Reality as a technology to support learning has generated new academic experiences and has promoted the inclusion of students with special educational needs, such as those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In the case of students with ASD, scientific research has confirmed the presence of difficulties in attention management. Therefore, the main objective of this study has been to apply Augmented Reality to improve the attention of students with ASD. To achieve this, a quantitative study was carried out with a quasi-experimental design without a control group, which included a participant with ASD level 3. The instrument used was a category system designed specifically for this study, which was applied during the 10 sessions that made up the intervention procedure. The results indicate that the student improved in the different types of attention worked on in most of the sessions in which Augmented Reality was used. In conclusion, the need for further research is evident, as this technology could be effective in improving the attention of these students.

articleTitle: Application of the Bee-Bot Robot to Improve the Oral Expression of a Student with ASD: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In recent decades, robotics has emerged as an appealing pedagogical tool capable of creating comprehensible and secure learning environments for students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), thereby enhancing various skills. ASD is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by difficulties in oral expression, such as challenges in language pragmatics, sound articulation, acquiring new words, or constructing complex sentences. Recognizing the potential of robotics in addressing the needs of these students, the present study aims to utilize the floor robot Bee-Bot in an educational context to improve the oral expression skills of a student with ASD. Regarding the methodology employed, a quantitative research approach was utilized, specifically a single-case quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test. Additionally, data collection involved a system of 19 categorized items distributed across 4 dimensions, and an intervention consisting of ten sessions with the Bee-Bot robot was implemented. The results have demonstrated significant improvements, with 78.94% of the questionnaire items showing positive changes following the implementation of robotics. In conclusion, it can be affirmed that the Bee-Bot robot, when accompanied by a pedagogical program, is a valuable educational resource for developing the oral expression of students with ASD.

articleTitle: Remind Tool as a Recommendation to Facilitate Communication with Parents
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: The reason for this research is to highlight the importance of the Remind App as a means of communication between teachers and parents. The methodology that was applied is of a descriptive nature with a quantitative approach, the data selection was carried out through the interview and survey techniques; 7 teachers and 14 parents from the “Escuela Benigno Bayancela” participated. A talk was held to expose the benefits offered by the application. The results show that teachers are open to using it due to its design and with parents there is fear and doubt to put it into practice even of the ICT functions, they do not agree to leave their comfort zone and the App requires access broadband Internet.

articleTitle: Identity, Gender and Connection
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article presents the pilot study on identity, gender and connection to digital platforms. A questionnaire of 11 questions about digital platforms and gender was applied to a population of students from the Universidad de Atacama. The first results indicate that most of the people indicated that digital platforms are media spaces that serve to express themselves among other issues that will be discussed in the presentation.

articleTitle: Edges of Educational Intervention in Mathematics Teaching: Incorporating ICT Beyond Gamification
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: This article addresses the problem of students' demotivation and rejection of mathematics in the classroom. We identified that in the educational experience, negative emotions are an essential cause of this problem. These have unfavorable consequences in the short, medium, and long term, such as low self-esteem, impact on academic performance, school and higher education dropout, reduced job opportunities, and negative impact on the development of a country. According to Ekman's theory of basic emotions, we propose a model to take advantage of the benefits of serious video games and mental sports to generate positive and pleasurable emotions. This solution will likely improve the educational experience in this subject and increase students' exercise, consequently improving their academic performance in mathematics.

articleTitle: Self-Efficacy to Train Computational Thinking Skills in Pre-Service Teachers*
publicationTitle: 2023 XIII International Conference on Virtual Campus (JICV)
abstract: In this work we, study the self-efficacy of the use of the Choreographe software in block programming using the NAO robot in order to develop instructional videos in the classroom within the framework of Computational Thinking. The put forward objectives were three; (1) Evaluate the level of significance of self-efficacy and the applicability of CT concepts.
